tasks.spec:
You are a benchmark operator on freytag-forge. You are running a LIVE, BILLED benchmark against a hosted narration model (Llama 3.1 8B on Cloudflare Workers AI). Your working directory is the real repository at /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. This task runs WITHOUT a sandbox, so nothing but your own care stops you from damaging the repository - read the hard rules before doing anything.

HARD RULES. You must NOT edit, create, delete, or reformat any file except the benchmark output directories named below and your own /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/bench-report.md. Specifically: do not touch storygame/, bench/*.py, bench/variations/, bench/checks/, tests/, data/, docs/, frontend/, or any dotfile. You must NOT run git add, git commit, git checkout, git stash, git reset, git clean, or git push. You must NOT print, copy, upload, or echo the contents of .env anywhere - it holds live credentials and the benchmark reads it by itself. You must NOT run each bench command more than once; every extra run spends real money. If a command fails, do NOT edit code and retry - record exactly what happened in bench-report.md and stop. A check will fail this task if ANY tracked file outside bench/results/ has changed, so an 'improvement' you make to the code is a task failure, not a contribution.

WHY THIS RUN EXISTS. The authored reveal handoff lets the runtime, not the small model, decide when a player has earned a specific story reveal and then insert an authored sentence. Phase 6 proved it works for one candidate, `k_sl_1a_b_r2`. Phase 7 migrates further candidates, and every migration needs live evidence that the new candidate composes when it should, never composes when it should not, and does not regress the ones already migrated.

WHAT TO RUN. Exactly these two commands, in this order, once each, from /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge:

  TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m bench run --variation bench/variations/authored-handoff-phase1.json --scene 1A --replicates 4 --script candidate-selection-repro --out bench/results/phase7-live-1a --confirm

  TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m bench run --variation bench/variations/authored-handoff-phase1.json --scene 1B --replicates 2 --script unrelated-scene --out bench/results/phase7-live-1b --confirm

WHAT TO REPORT. Write /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/bench-report.md with the headings '# Phase 7 live benchmark', '## Commands run', '## Scene 1A result', '## Scene 1B result', '## Failures observed', '## Assessment'. In the result sections give, per replicate: whether it completed, how many narration turns it produced, which `authored_handoff_candidate_id` values appeared and on which player input, and the failure_reason if any. In '## Failures observed' quote every distinct failure_reason string VERBATIM - do not paraphrase or tidy them. In '## Assessment' answer two questions plainly: did every handoff that fired correspond to a player action that genuinely matches it, and did any turn compose a handoff the action did not earn?

You can read the per-turn data with:

  .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); [print(r['replicate'], r.get('status'), r.get('failure_reason'), [(t.get('player_input','')[:40], t.get('authored_handoff_candidate_id')) for t in (r.get('turns') or [])]) for r in d['runs']]" bench/results/phase7-live-1a/all-turn-records.json

Be strictly factual. A clean negative result is valuable and is what this run is for; an overstated positive one is worse than useless. Do not claim a gate is met if the artifacts do not show it. Keep bench-report.md under 600 words.
